Max severity SonicWall SMA1000 flaw now exploited in attacks — Must Read

Attackers are attempting to exploit the newly patched maximum-severity CVE-2026-102255 SSRF flaw in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances, potentially reaching internal services and performing unauthorized actions. Organizations using affected SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v devices should apply SonicWall’s patch immediately.

  • Attackers are attempting to exploit CVE-2026-102255, a maximum-severity flaw in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances that SonicWall patched three days before the report.
  • The flaw affects the Appliance WorkPlace interface on SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v models, but not the SMA 100 Series or SSL-VPN on SonicWall firewalls.
  • Previdian detected requests targeting the WorkPlace Extraweb interface that attempted to reach the appliance’s internal CouchDB service using a crafted OPTIONS request and admin:admin credentials.
  • SonicWall SMA1000 gateways are used by managed service providers, large corporations, and government agencies for access to internal applications and networks.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 400 SMA1000 appliances exposed online, although the number that are patched or honeypots is unknown.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access, database

Products: sonicwall-sma1000, appliance-workplace, couchdb

Vendors: sonicwall, apache

Flax Typhoon Exploits Five Flaws as CISA Sets October 11 Deadline for Federal Agencies — Must Read

CISA added five actively exploited flaws tied to China-linked Flax Typhoon to its KEV catalog, including vulnerabilities in ProFTPD, ONLYOFFICE Docs, Strapi, Apache Struts, and ISC BIND. U.S. federal agencies must patch or discontinue affected products by October 11, 2026.

  • CISA added five vulnerabilities associated with Flax Typhoon activity to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • The newly added flaws affect ProFTPD, ONLYOFFICE Docs, Strapi, Apache Struts, and ISC BIND.
  • A joint advisory from Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States said a China-based company called Integrity Technology Group enabled operations targeting eight vulnerabilities.
  • The reported activity used scanning tools, cross-site scripting, and password spraying against Microsoft Exchange servers to gain access, while scripts were used to steal emails and credentials.
  • U.S. federal agencies must patch the affected vulnerabilities or stop using the affected products by October 11, 2026.

New GhostAction Wave Hits Hundreds of Repos, Expanding Beyond CI/CD Secrets to Cloud Credentials — Must Read

A new GhostAction campaign used compromised GitHub maintainer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows into 346 repositories, stealing configured CI/CD secrets and scanning current files plus full Git history for cloud and AI credentials. Organizations should remove the workflow, rotate exposed credentials, investigate workflow runs and egress to the hardcoded collector IP, and secure affected maintainer accounts.

  • On October 8, 2026, compromised GitHub accounts henrywoo and kitao added a malicious .github/workflows/security-audit.yml file to 346 repositories, including uber/athenadriver and kitao/pyxel.
  • The workflow runs on pushes and can collect GitHub Actions secrets named in existing workflows before sending them to the hardcoded IP address 193.32.204[.]199.
  • This GhostAction variant also searches checked-out files and complete reachable Git history for AWS, AI-service, source-control, SaaS, and cloud API credentials.
  • The workflow uses a full Git checkout and context around AWS key identifiers to capture nearby information that may include corresponding secret access keys.
  • Socket reported that the malicious workflow remained on the default branches it checked as of October 9, 2026, and it had not observed malicious package releases to PyPI or crates.io at that time.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, package-registry, cloud-platform

Products: github-actions, github, pypi, crates-io

Vendors: github, socket, gitguardian, amazon-web-services, openai, anthropic, openrouter, gitlab, google, slack, sendgrid

The Phishing Page Printed the Visitor's Own Location — May Read

A French bank-themed phishing email passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and received clean URL verdicts because its landing page served different anti-analysis responses based on CAPTCHA and visitor location. The key takeaway is that a clean URL scan reflects only what the phishing kit showed that scanner at that moment, not whether the destination is safe.

  • A European aerospace and industrial engineering firm received three French device-renewal phishing emails on 15 May 2026 that impersonated Crédit Agricole.
  • Captures of the same landing URL taken two days apart showed different responses: a Crédit Agricole-branded CAPTCHA page and a French geo-restriction page that displayed the visitor’s detected country and IP address.
  • The landing domain portail-client-mail[.]net was not a Crédit Agricole domain, and the article states that Crédit Agricole was an uninvolved brand impersonation target.
  • SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication passed because the emails were sent through an abused bulk-mail account belonging to a US technical college.
  • IRONSCALES Themis classified the incident as credential theft with 88 confidence and recorded all three messages as mitigated within seconds of delivery.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: themis, amazon-s3

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, amazon

Man admits to running network of 15,000 money mules for cybercriminals — May Read

Ukrainian-Russian dual citizen Oleg Korniev pleaded guilty to leading Your Mule Cashout, an international operation that recruited more than 15,000 U.S. money mules and laundered millions in cybercrime proceeds. The scheme caused over $14.7 million in actual and intended victim losses, and Korniev faces up to 50 years in prison.

  • Ukrainian-Russian dual citizen Oleg Korniev pleaded guilty to charges including money laundering, aggravated identity theft, computer fraud conspiracy, and access-device theft conspiracy.
  • Korniev was a leader of Your Mule Cashout, an organization active since September 2007 that used more than 15,000 money mules in the United States.
  • Your Mule Cashout recruited U.S. residents through spam emails posing as legitimate companies and instructed them to process payments that were actually stolen funds.
  • The operation processed more than $10 million stolen from over 750 U.S. bank accounts at more than 35 banks and was linked to more than $14.7 million in actual and intended losses.
  • Korniev admitted laundering at least $7 million of the $9.7 million received from cybercriminals and faces a prison sentence ranging from two to 50 years.

Vendors: western-union, moneygram

The AI Velocity Paradox: Why Security Is Decades Behind AI Ambition — Optional

SailPoint’s report argues that enterprises are adopting autonomous AI agents faster than their identity security can govern them, leaving non-human identities managed by human-speed, manual controls. Organizations need continuous, automated, machine-speed access governance to close this gap.

  • SailPoint’s Horizons of Identity Security report says organizations are adopting autonomous AI agents while relying on security controls designed for human-operated processes.
  • The report states that 60% of organizations remain in either the “No Formal Program” or “Manual, Tool-Assisted” identity-security maturity stages.
  • Human identity security has improved over five years, with the share of organizations at the lowest maturity level declining from 45% to 23%.
  • For non-human and AI agent identities, 54% of organizations are currently at the lowest maturity level, according to the report.
  • The report argues that organizations need continuous, contextual, automated policy enforcement rather than manual, ticket-based access decisions to operate at machine speed.

Technologies: iam

Vendors: sailpoint

Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments — Must Read

Citrix patched CVE-2026-107406, a critical NetScaler ADC and Gateway memory-overflow flaw that can enable remote code execution or denial of service when SAML IdP or SP functionality is configured. Organizations should upgrade affected NetScaler appliances to the latest fixed releases; no active exploitation has been reported.

  • Citrix released patches for CVE-2026-107406, a critical memory-overflow flaw in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway with a CVSS score of 9.5.
  • Under specific configurations, CVE-2026-107406 may allow remote code execution or denial of service.
  • The flaw affects NetScaler deployments configured as a SAML identity provider or service provider, including Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments that use NetScaler instances.
  • Citrix recommends upgrading to NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.46 or later, 13.1-64.29 or later, or the corresponding fixed FIPS and NDcPP releases.
  • Citrix said there is no evidence that CVE-2026-107406 has been exploited in the wild.

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway, secure-private-access-hybrid

FBI Seizes 7 Domains, Disrupts Flax Typhoon Tools Used in Critical Infrastructure Intrusions — Should Read

The FBI and DOJ seized seven domains used by China-linked Flax Typhoon and Integrity Technology Group to operate reconnaissance and spear-phishing tools targeting U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure. The action follows disruption of the group’s Raptor Train IoT botnet and highlights its continued use of large-scale scanning, botnets, and credential theft.

  • The FBI and U.S. Department of Justice seized seven domains used by China-linked Flax Typhoon to support vulnerability scanning, spear-phishing, and, in some cases, intrusions targeting critical infrastructure.
  • Flax Typhoon, also known as Ethereal Panda and RedJuliett, is associated with Beijing-based Integrity Technology Group, which U.S. authorities say contracted with the Chinese government.
  • Integrity Technology Group allegedly operated the Raptor Train IoT botnet using a Mirai variant; as of June 5, 2024, records showed more than 1.2 million infected devices, including more than 385,000 unique U.S. devices.
  • The group’s MicroScan tool included more than 1,300 penetration-testing scripts and was used alongside other tools to identify weaknesses in networks and web applications.
  • Authorities said the group targeted organizations including a U.S. power company, airports in Japan and Poland, Taiwanese natural-gas and power companies, and Taiwanese universities.

Technologies: vpn, cloud-platform, iot-device

Products: microscan, fishhub, softether-vpn, microsoft-365

Vendors: integrity-technology-group, microsoft, softether-project

GoBalance Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack .onion Addresses by Recovering Tor-Format Keys — Should Read

A flaw in GoBalance can expose a Tor hidden service’s long-term private key from a public descriptor, allowing attackers to hijack its .onion address and redirect visitors. Affected operators must migrate to a newly generated address because patching cannot revoke keys already exposed.

  • A flaw in GoBalance can allow someone to recover the private key controlling a Tor .onion address from a single publicly available service descriptor and redirect visitors to an attacker-controlled site.
  • The issue stems from GoBalance passing only the first 32 bytes of a 64-byte Tor private key to its signing process, making a normally secret signature value predictable.
  • The original Onionbalance software and Tor itself are not affected, and GoBalance sites using the safer key format created by its setup tool are not exposed.
  • Dread reported that both of its .onion addresses were taken over between October 5 and 7, while Omega said it moved away from its old address because of the GoBalance bug.
  • Patching GoBalance cannot protect a key that was already exposed, so affected operators must generate and migrate to a new .onion address.

Technologies: load-balancer

Products: gobalance, onionbalance, endgame, tor

Vendors: tor-project, gobalance, searchlight-cyber

Three Teams Demonstrate Remote Hacks of Fully Patched Google Pixel 10 at Pwn2Own — Should Read

Three teams remotely compromised fully patched Google Pixel 10 phones at Pwn2Own Ireland, earning a combined $562,500 and exposing flaws that Google will receive for patching. Technical details remain undisclosed during the vendor remediation period.

  • Ikotas Labs received $300,000 and 30 points for its Pixel 10 exploit chain and was named Master of Pwn after four contest wins.
  • Xint received $150,000 for a Pixel 10 entry involving a single previously known issue, while Dimitrios Valsamaras, Ken Gannon, and Tenia Valsamara received $112,500 for a two-bug chain containing one previously known issue and one newly discovered issue.
  • The technical details and attack routes for the Pixel 10 demonstrations had not been published as of October 9, and vendors have 90 days to release patches before ZDI publishes full details.
  • All seven Galaxy S26 attempts succeeded, and 51 of the 63 scheduled attempts across the contest succeeded.

What the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report reveals about AI, identity, and the future of cybersecurity — Optional

Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report underscores that identity sprawl, cloud permissions, non-human accounts, and AI agents create interconnected attack paths that inventories alone cannot reveal. Organizations should use graph-based attack path management to identify shared privilege choke points and reduce technical debt before AI-enabled attackers can find and exploit it faster.

  • Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report says that cloud identity abuse appeared in 78% of observed critical-infrastructure activity.
  • The report states that inventories alone are insufficient and that graph-based mapping is needed to show how identities, permissions, automation, and resources connect.
  • Microsoft reports that 88% of enterprises are experimenting with AI agents, which can accumulate excessive access and add new identities and dependencies to organizational environments.
  • AzureHound appeared in 12% of the observed tool mix used against critical infrastructure for mapping cloud attack paths, according to the article.
  • Attack Path Management can identify shared relationships across many potential attack paths, allowing a focused remediation to close multiple paths at once.

item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Oct 18:00 → 08 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Suspected TraderTraitor Group Uses Trojanized Terraform Provider to Deliver Cross-Platform Malware — Should Read

Zscaler researchers found a suspected North Korean TraderTraitor campaign that trojanized a Terraform provider to silently deploy FLATROOF credential-stealing malware and the ROOFDECK backdoor across macOS, Linux, and Windows. The campaign targets developer workflows and uses disguised font files, public hosting, and resilient Pastebin/Nostr-based C2 discovery to evade detection.

  • ThreatLabz identified a trojanized Terraform provider named terraform-provider-awsbeta_v1.0.0 that preserves normal Terraform behavior while downloading and launching a Bash loader from a HashiCorp-themed lookalike domain.
  • The Bash loader selects encrypted payloads for macOS, Linux, or Windows based on the victim system’s operating system and processor architecture, disguising the payloads as .woff font files.
  • The delivered FLATROOF Rust-based backdoor uses platform-specific persistence and can communicate through Telegram, GitHub, or an attacker-controlled HTTP webhook.
  • FLATROOF includes Python data-stealing scripts that collect browser credentials, cookies, browsing artifacts, shell history, system information, and, on Windows, data associated with several cryptocurrency wallet extensions.
  • The related ROOFDECK backdoor uses a local configuration file, a signed encrypted Pastebin record, and Nostr profile metadata to locate its command-and-control server.

Technologies: orchestration, ci-cd, source-control, cloud-platform

Products: terraform, terraform-provider-aws, github, telegram-bot-api, pastebin

Vendors: hashicorp, github, zscaler, vercel, telegram, pastebin

International coalition seizes tools used by cyber firm behind Flax Typhoon — Should Read

An international coalition led by the U.S. seized Microscan and FishHub, hacking tools operated by Chinese firm Integrity Tech to support Flax Typhoon espionage against critical infrastructure and other global targets. Authorities say the company enabled Chinese state-linked actors with scanning, phishing, botnet, and data-theft capabilities.

  • The U.S. Justice Department seized websites supporting Microscan and FishHub, tools operated by Beijing-based Integrity Tech and used in activity linked to the Flax Typhoon campaign.
  • Authorities said Microscan has been used since 2017 to scan websites for specific weaknesses, with reported targets including a South Carolina power company, airports in Japan and Poland, and Taiwanese power and natural-gas organizations.
  • FishHub was designed to speed up deceptive-email operations and was used to provide remote access after breaches, including against about 20 universities in Taiwan.
  • The FBI, CISA, and NSA said Integrity Tech and associated Chinese groups often targeted poorly monitored network-edge devices to retain long-term hidden access to organizations.
  • U.S. agencies previously disrupted a Mirai-based Flax Typhoon botnet of more than 260,000 consumer devices in September 2024.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: microscan, fishhub, eburst, microsoft-exchange-server

Vendors: integrity-tech, microsoft

Ransomware attack disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud used by govt clients — Should Read

IDC Frontier's IDCF Cloud suffered a ransomware attack that forced it to shut down systems in its East Japan Region 1 cluster, affecting 495 companies and local governments. The attackers claim to have encrypted databases and VM disks and deleted more than 554,000 snapshots, while the provider investigates the intrusion and restores services.

  • IDC Frontier said a ransomware attack began at 3:40 AM local time on October 7 and caused an outage in its IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1 cluster.
  • The company shut down affected network and system infrastructure to contain the incident, and it has disabled customer access to management consoles in all regions while checking their security.
  • IDC Frontier said the incident affects 495 companies and local governments that use its cloud service.
  • A message seen by customers claimed that the attackers encrypted 225 databases, reached 239 hypervisors, sealed 16,000 virtual-machine disks, and wiped 554,153 snapshots.
  • Nissui Logistics reported an outage at a third-party data center that has halted goods shipments and receipts, although its connection to the IDCF Cloud incident is unclear.

Technologies: cloud-platform, hypervisor, database, backup

Products: idcf-cloud

Vendors: idc-frontier, softbank-group

Low-cost Android phones ship with residential proxy malware — Should Read

Bitdefender found Midnight Mimosa malware preinstalled in the firmware of low-cost MediaTek Android phones, giving attackers system-level control to install apps, commit ad fraud, and potentially use devices as residential proxies. The supply-chain source remains unknown, and removal generally requires a clean firmware update or advanced ADB intervention.

  • Bitdefender identified the Midnight Mimosa campaign as malware embedded in the firmware of low-cost MediaTek-based Android devices, where it runs with system-level privileges.
  • The campaign affected thousands of devices in more than 150 countries over roughly two years, with the largest victim counts reported in Mexico, France, Italy, the United States, Germany, Brazil, and Spain.
  • Midnight Mimosa can silently install and remove apps, temporarily disable the Google Play Store before installations, and alter installer records to make malicious apps appear to come from Google Play.
  • The malware's downloaded apps conduct advertising fraud through hidden windows and automated ad interactions, while one app-locker-disguised component can register phones as TCP residential proxies.
  • Because the malicious software is installed as a privileged system app, Bitdefender said removal requires firmware-level cleanup or disabling the component through Android Debug Bridge.

Technologies: mobile-os, proxy

Products: android, google-play-store, google-play-protect, doogee-s200-x, cubot-kingkong-x, doogee-fire-3-max

Vendors: bitdefender, google, mediatek, doogee, cubot, shenzhen-zediel, fivedev, cps-developer

Lawmakers warn Google could expose Spirit Airlines data in $10 million AI training deal — May Read

More than 100 U.S. lawmakers urged Google and defunct Spirit Airlines to halt a proposed $10 million sale of de-identified employee data for AI training, warning that modern AI could re-identify workers. The dataset reportedly includes hundreds of millions of internal messages and sensitive employment, payroll, and tax records.

  • A group of 114 U.S. lawmakers urged Google and Spirit Airlines to halt a proposed $10 million deal to provide Google with internal Spirit data for AI training.
  • The proposed data sale would include approximately 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages, employment contracts, employee timecard records, and payroll and tax information.
  • Google has said the data would be de-identified and scrubbed by a third party before transfer, but lawmakers said removing direct identifiers may not make the dataset anonymous.
  • The lawmakers recommended that, if the deal proceeds, Google and Spirit seek former employees’ feedback, exclude as much employee data as possible, limit use of the data, and conduct an independent employee confidentiality review.
  • Spirit announced plans to shut down in May, and nearly 1,000 people lost their jobs in parts of Las Vegas represented by Representative Steven Horsford.

Products: microsoft-teams

Vendors: google, microsoft

StepSecurity Now Inventories AI Agent Skills in Your GitHub Repositories and on Developer Machines — Optional

StepSecurity launched Agent Skills inventory capabilities that identify AI-agent skills on developer machines and in GitHub repositories, helping teams find skills with executable code, hooks, shell commands, or pre-approved tools. The feature aims to reduce supply-chain risk from repository-distributed or unmanaged skills that can run with developer privileges.

  • StepSecurity added Agent Skills inventories in Dev Machine Guard for developer machines and under GitHub for skills committed to an organization’s GitHub.com repositories.
  • Agent skills are folders containing a SKILL.md file and optional scripts or resources that AI coding agents can load, and some can execute scripts, use hooks, or pre-approve tools.
  • Dev Machine Guard scans supported shared, agent-specific, project-level, plugin-provided, and skills.sh-managed skill locations across 18 AI coding agents.
  • The GitHub Agent Skills page scans the default branch of each non-archived GitHub.com repository daily and identifies skills in supported folders, including their source, executable-content flags, file counts, and scripts.
  • StepSecurity recommends reviewing skills with shell execution, hooks, or code; checking pre-approved tools and managed-skill origins; and comparing differing or unmanaged copies found on developer devices.

Technologies: source-control

Products: dev-machine-guard, agent-skills, github, claude-code, codex, skills-sh, cline, openclaw

Vendors: stepsecurity, github, anthropic, openai, microsoft, nx

Making sure the checks get printed — Optional

Cisco Talos warns that malware authors are embedding natural-language prompt injections in code to manipulate AI-assisted malware analysis, sometimes steering verdicts in the attacker’s favor. Defenders should treat extracted sample text only as untrusted evidence and detect suspicious instructions aimed at analysis systems.

  • Cisco Talos reports that malware authors are embedding natural-language instructions in code to evade AI-assisted analysis, a trend it calls "A3: AI-Analysis Evasion."
  • Talos observed techniques over the past 18 months ranging from comments telling an AI to ignore a file to template spraying intended to mislead specific large language models.
  • Talos found that these prompt-injection techniques steer an AI verdict in the attacker’s favor about 35 percent of the time and are used across different levels of malware sophistication.
  • The MANTLEMAZE family combines AI-analysis deception with abuse of vulnerable drivers to disable endpoint detection and response software from kernel space.
  • Talos recommends treating text extracted from a sample strictly as evidence rather than as a system directive and flagging imperative language addressed to analysis systems within binaries.

Technologies: load-balancer, edr

Products: cisco-talos, netscaler

Vendors: cisco, citrix, google

UAC-0099 Targets Ukrainian Government Personnel With ASHVEIN RAT Hiding Commands in HTML — Must Read

Russia-aligned UAC-0099 is targeting Ukrainian government and logistics personnel with the newly documented ASHVEIN .NET RAT, which steals browser credentials, captures screenshots, collects files, and receives concealed commands through HTML. The group continues evolving its tooling and delivery methods, including DLL sideloading, VHD containers, and decoy documents impersonating Ukrainian institutions.

  • TrendAI attributed the previously undocumented ASHVEIN .NET information stealer and remote-access tool to the Russia-aligned UAC-0099 group, which it tracks as Earth Sirrush.
  • ASHVEIN can steal Chrome and Firefox credentials, capture screenshots, list and retrieve files, execute remote PowerShell commands, fingerprint systems, and communicate with its operators using encryption.
  • UAC-0099 has delivered ASHVEIN through DLL sideloading, VHD containers, and .NET droppers, including AnswerFromPolice, which displays a decoy document impersonating the National Police of Ukraine.
  • UAC-0099 has targeted Ukrainian government, defense, border guard, and logistics entities since at least mid-2022, and available evidence indicates its targeting has expanded to civilian logistics and infrastructure operators.
  • The group has expanded and changed its malware toolkit over time, moving from PowerShell- and Go-based tools toward compiled C# and .NET Reactor-protected programs concealed in image files.

Technologies: browser, source-control, remote-access

Products: microsoft-word, github, google-chrome, mozilla-firefox

Vendors: trend-ai, eset, microsoft, google, mozilla

Japan Sees Sharp Rise in Web Data Leaks Amid Mobile API Abuse and Metabase Attacks — Should Read

JPCERT/CC warns that a surge in Japanese personal-data leaks is tied to mobile API abuse, weak access controls, exposed administrative systems, and exploitation of the critical Metabase SQL injection flaw CVE-2026-72898. Organizations should urgently patch Metabase, review logs and API access, rotate exposed credentials, and enforce endpoint-level authorization and rate limits.

  • JPCERT/CC warned that attackers behind recent personal-data leaks at Japanese organizations have abused mobile-app APIs, targeted known software flaws, and accessed systems not expected to be publicly reachable.
  • Macnica counted 119 publicly disclosed Japanese web-system incidents involving stolen or leaked personal data through October 6, 2026, with 81 reported from July onward.
  • Park24 said that data from about 6.6 million Times Car accounts was obtained by a third party, and that identity documents from about 1.6 million accounts had leaked.
  • JPCERT/CC identified exploitation of CVE-2026-72898, a critical unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Metabase that can enable administrator access and access to credentials for connected databases.
  • JPCERT/CC recommended rate limits, access controls for every API endpoint, least-privilege API tokens, token expiration, and rapid token revocation to reduce API abuse.

Products: metabase

Vendors: metabase

Cisco warns of critical flaws allowing Nexus switch takeover — Should Read

Cisco disclosed five critical NX-OS flaws that can let attackers execute code as root or cause denial of service on affected Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches when NX-API, NGOAM, or MPLS OAM features are enabled. Organizations should upgrade to Cisco’s fixed releases or disable unneeded features and use temporary Live Protect shields where patching is delayed.

  • Cisco disclosed five critical NX-OS vulnerabilities that could allow arbitrary code execution with root privileges or cause denial of service on affected Nexus switches.
  • The flaws affect Nexus 3000 and Nexus 9000 Series switches running standalone NX-OS when NX-API, Next Generation OAM, or MPLS OAM features are enabled.
  • NX-API and MPLS OAM are disabled by default, while the three NGOAM-related vulnerabilities require NGOAM to be enabled.
  • Cisco recommends upgrading to fixed NX-OS releases, disabling unneeded affected features, or using temporary Live Protect shields when immediate upgrades and reboots are not possible.
  • Cisco said the vulnerabilities were found during internal testing and that it was not aware of public disclosure or malicious exploitation when the advisories were published.

Technologies: switch, operating-system

Products: nx-os, nexus-3000, nexus-9000, cisco-license

Vendors: cisco

Leaked chats show Russian extortion gang sending ‘agents’ into US law firms — Should Read

Leaked chats linked to the Russia-based Silent Ransom Group indicate it recruited U.S.-based “agents” to physically infiltrate law firms, steal data and support multimillion-dollar extortion demands. The archive also contains unverified discussions of more extreme schemes targeting executives and U.S. military personnel.

  • A leaked archive of chats from August 2025 to September 2026 appears to document activities of the Russia-based Silent Ransom Group, also tracked as Luna Moth and Chatty Spider.
  • Chainalysis linked cryptocurrency addresses in the archive to known Silent Ransom Group extortions, while cautioning that it could not verify all claims in the leaked chats.
  • The chats describe recruiting U.S.-based “agents” through Telegram job advertisements to impersonate delivery workers, clients, or IT personnel and gain physical access to law firm offices.
  • The FBI previously warned that Silent Ransom Group members had posed as IT personnel to access computers at law firms, and one negotiation in the archive involved a New York office where files were reportedly copied onto a flash drive.
  • The archive records claimed settlements totaling roughly $200 million across dozens of organizations, mostly law firms, but those figures could not be independently verified.

Products: telegram

FakeGit malware campaign returns with 17,610 malicious GitHub repos — Should Read

The phone was compromised before the user turned it on: the rise of Midnight Mimosa — Should Read

Bitdefender uncovered Midnight Mimosa, a preinstalled Android malware family on low-cost MediaTek devices that runs with system privileges, silently installs payloads, commits ad fraud, and can turn phones into residential proxy botnet nodes. Because the core component is embedded in firmware and cannot normally be removed, affected users may need a clean vendor firmware replacement or device replacement.

  • Bitdefender identified Midnight Mimosa as a malware campaign preinstalled in the firmware of some low-cost, MediaTek-based Android devices, before users first power them on.
  • The persistent system application uses system-level privileges to silently install and remove apps, grant permissions, and load code supplied remotely.
  • The campaign’s dropped apps conduct hidden advertising and click fraud and can enroll devices as residential-proxy relay nodes controlled through a remote server.
  • Researchers observed the malware disabling the Google Play Store before installing payload apps and re-enabling it afterward, apparently to evade Play Protect scanning.
  • Bitdefender also identified 13 Google Play applications that share ad-fraud code and command infrastructure with the campaign’s dropped cover apps.

Cisco Talos uncovered UAT-11985, a targeted campaign against Taiwanese research organizations that uses AI-assisted event invitations, tampered QR-code posters, and real-time Google adversary-in-the-middle phishing to steal credentials, MFA responses, and authenticated sessions.

  • Cisco Talos observed UAT-11985, a spear-phishing campaign targeting individuals affiliated with Taiwan-based research organizations in mid-2026.
  • The campaign impersonated Taiwanese academic and policy institutions, reused legitimate event information, and used misleading registration links that redirected victims to actor-controlled phishing sites.
  • The actor attached legitimate-looking event posters with maliciously modified QR codes, creating an additional route to phishing pages for people who scanned the posters.
  • The phishing kit imitated Google sign-in pages in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English and used HTTP POST requests and WebSocket connections to relay authentication steps in real time.
  • Talos assessed with moderate confidence that the phishing kit’s interface was originally developed in Simplified Chinese before being adapted for Traditional Chinese and English.

Russian-aligned UAC-0099 is continually upgrading its MatchBoil malware to target Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy organizations through phishing campaigns. The malware profiles infected systems, establishes persistence, and can deploy additional tools including the MatchWok backdoor and Dragstare information stealer.

  • ESET linked the MatchBoil malware to UAC-0099, a cyberespionage group it believes is likely working in Russia’s interests, and said all observed infections were in Ukraine.

  • The malware can collect information about an infected machine, download additional malicious software from an attacker-controlled server, and remain active on the system.

A phishing campaign used a compromised credential on a Korean shared email host to send authenticated, SPF-passing messages impersonating victims’ own employer, with the provider’s X-Authinfo header exposing the mismatched attacker login. The embedded Microsoft OAuth link was a silent identity-reconnaissance probe rather than a mailbox-token theft attempt, highlighting why authentication checks alone cannot detect account takeover abuse.

  • A Korean shared business-mail provider’s X-Authinfo header showed that an account at one Korean company authenticated the SMTP session while the message was sent as an address at an unrelated Korean company.
  • The phishing message passed SPF and was delivered to recipients’ inboxes despite having no DKIM signature, because the shared mail host was authorized to send for the impersonated company’s domain.
  • The lure impersonated the recipients’ own employer and claimed that a contract document requiring a signature had been shared only with people inside the victim’s domain.
  • Its Microsoft authorization link used prompt=none with only openid, profile, and email scopes, and the captured response returned AADSTS50058/login_required rather than evidence of mailbox-token theft.
  • Four senior legal and commercial mailboxes at a multinational coffee and consumer-goods group were targeted between November 18 and December 2, 2025, and all four messages were quarantined.

Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware — Optional

Cisco Talos finds malware authors increasingly embedding plaintext prompt-injection strings to manipulate AI-assisted malware analysis, but the simplest direct instructions only inconsistently steer models and are readily detectable. Defenders should treat all text extracted from samples as untrusted evidence rather than executable instructions.

  • Cisco Talos tracked 84 samples across four confirmed AI-analysis-evasion malware families—FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, and MANTLEMAZE—collected from January 2025 through July 2026.

  • HOLLOWCLAD and MANTLEMAZE used multiple AI chat-template formats to try to match the format used by an analysis system, while also including misleading claims intended to deter analysis.
  • Talos found that direct instructions to ignore a sample had the strongest steering effect in its tests, but effects were mixed overall and the plaintext strings provide a stable detection surface for defenders.

Although Mozilla removed the extensions, anyone who entered wallet credentials should treat them as compromised and move assets to a newly created wallet from a clean system.

  • As of October 5, 2026, all identified extensions had been removed, but users who entered real recovery phrases or private keys were advised to consider them compromised and move assets to a new wallet created from a clean system.
  • The campaign was assessed as a continuation of an earlier wave, with operators changing extension names and presentation details while reusing wallet interfaces, credential-handling code, and network infrastructure.

Organizations that installed it should treat affected hosts as compromised, remove persistence before revoking tokens, and rebuild systems from trusted sources.

  • Organizations that installed tensorlake@0.5.144 are advised to isolate affected hosts, remove the gh-token-monitor persistence mechanism before revoking tokens, rotate exposed credentials, and rebuild affected environments from trusted sources.

Zscaler researchers found a suspected North Korean TraderTraitor campaign using a trojanized Terraform provider to silently deliver FLATROOF and ROOFDECK malware to macOS, Linux, and Windows developer systems. Leaked chats linked to the Russia-based Silent Ransom Group describe a campaign to recruit U.S.-based operatives to physically infiltrate law firms and steal data for extortion.
